City Manager de Geus announced two internal promotions: Mr. Tim Iverson was
promoted from Lead Public Works Inspector to Public Works Manager and Ms. Megan
Sinkula from Associate Planner to Senior Planner. He noted that both staff members
have demonstrated excellent service to the City, are highly competent and are always
willing to help and assist wherever they can to resolve resident issues. He asked the
Council to join him in congratulating both Tim and Megan on their promotions.

Mr. de Geus also mentioned that woodchips are being replenished in our City Parks as
part of our annual maintenance. Berniece Bennett, Canyon Oaks, Three Springs and
Foxfield parks received the new natural woodchips. This is done annually to ensure our
parks are clean, safe and enjoyed by everyone that visits them.

together with Deputy City Manager Eskandar for the 4th Grade Classes at White Oak

1.  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT  NO.  12-001,  MODIFICATION  NO.  2 .I
  RESOLUTION NO. 2241-22

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and Senior Planner Sinkula presented  ~
  the request to adopt a Resolution approving an extension of the expiration date for
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 12-001 to authorize the continued operation of
  an animal hospital located at 30849 Thousand Oaks Boulevard.

  Ms. Sinkula reported that CUP 12-001 was originally approved on February 8,
  2012. An additional five-year permit extension was approved on September 11,
  2017 with an expiration date of February 8, 2022. She reported that the applicant,
  Banfield Pet Hospital doing business as Dr. Y's Animal Hospital, will continue the
  operation with no proposed modifications to the permit which allows for a full-
  service veterinary care operation with no outdoor components on the site and no
  boarding services. She mentioned that the operating hours are Mondays -
  Fridays, 8:00 am to 6:00 pm, and Saturdays, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm., with five to ten
  employees on site. She noted that although the animal hospital has changed
  ownership, the operation of the facility has remained the same and staff was not
  aware of any negative impacts or complaints associated with the business. She
  recommended that the permit be approved for an additional 10 years.

  Ms. Sinkula added that on March 2, 2022, the Land Use Committee, Mayor Pro
  Tern Pearl and Councilmember Honig, reviewed the request and recommended
  that the time extension be moved forward to the full City Council for hearing.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved that Resolution No. 2241-22, 'A Resolution of
  the City Council of the City of Westlake Village approving an extension of the
  expiration date for Conditional Use Permit No. 12-001 to authorize the continued
  operation of an animal hospital located at 30849 Thousand Oaks Boulevard' be
  adopted. Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.

  YES :  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl, and Mayor Halpern
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

  2. ADOPTION OF URGENCY ORDINANCE AND INTRODUCTION OF
  ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 5.3 OF THE WESTLAKE VILLAGE  =-l
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT;
  URGENCY ORDINANCE NO. 290U-22 AND ORDINANCE NO. 291-22

  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and Planning Director Forbes
  presented the item, stating that Senate Bill (SB) 1383 and SB 619 action taken by
  the City Council on February 23, 2022 stipulated that the City would be adopting a
  mandatory recycling and organics Ordinance by April 1, 2022.

  Mr. Forbes explained that SB 1383 requires the diversion of organic waste from
  landfills to reduce methane emission. Organic waste includes green waste
  (landscape trimming, plants and wood), food scraps and soiled paper. Cities must
  comply and strictly enforce their Ordinance starting January 2024. He added that
  the proposed Ordinance will include new organic waste collection requirements,
  with Waste Management providing new bins for all customers as part of the
  updated hauler agreement. He noted that the current ordinance provides for an
  exclusive hauler for residential but not commercial service; however, the proposed
  ordinance includes an exclusive hauler clause for residential and commercial
  services. Existing haulers will be phased out over a five-year period to ensure
  compliance with reporting and enforcement of SB 1383 standards.

  There was Council discussion on whether an urgency Ordinance was warranted
  and the addition of the "exclusivity clause" to the Ordinance in Section 5.3.070.

  Ms. Carrie Baxter, R3 Consulting Group, attending via Zoom, reported that the
  state requirement was to have an Ordinance by January 1, 2022 and the
  mechanisms to enforce the ordinance by April 1, 2022. Without the mechanisms
  in place, the City could be fined up to $10,000 a day by CalRecycle. Additionally,
  Ms. Baxter reported that the City will not be able to apply for any grants related to
  SB 1383 implementation without the Ordinance being in effect by April 1, 2022.

  Mr. Forbes reported that the State is offering non-competitive grants, based on
  population, making Westlake Village eligible for a $20,000 grant. When Council
  adopted the resolution on February 23, 2022, the City indicated to CalRecycle that
  an Ordinance would be adopted by April 1, 2022.

  There was Council discussion on how often urgency ordinances are adopted. City
  Attorney Boga provided information on Urgency Ordinances.
   City Council Minutes

l  There was further Council discussion on the five-year phase-out time period for
  commercial haulers. Mr. Forbes responded that State Law requires the five-year
  phasing out period for non-exclusive haulers and that staff added this clause to our
  ordinance to assist with SB 1383 compliance.

  With regard to the current Waste Management contract, Mr. Forbes stated that the
  contract is still in the negotiation process, but Council should be aware that the
  overall pricing structure for residential and commercial customers is based upon
  the assumption that they will receive commercial exclusivity in five-years.

  Mayor Pro Tern Pearl inquired if removal of the exclusivity section in the ordinance
  will impact the ability to obtain the best pricing on the waste hauler agreement.
  Mr. Forbes indicated that residential and commercial rates would likely be higher
  without the exclusivity clause because of the economy of scale. City Manager de
  Geus informed the Council that when the hauler agreement is brought before the
  Council for approval, the ordinance could be amended, if necessary, to reflect the
  terms approved by the Council. City Attorney Boga also clarified that the ordinance
  can be subsequently amended.
